title: Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs
summary: Let $C_n^k$ denote the $k$th power of the cycle $C_n$. The equivalence covering number $\operatorname{eq}(G)$, studied by Alon, is the minimum number of equivalence subgraphs needed to cover all edges of $G$. King conjectured that $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)=Ω(k)$ for sufficiently large $n$ relative to $k$. We study $\operatorname{eq}(C_n^k)$ and prove that, for every $n \geq 2k + 2$, we have $1 + \lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil \leq \operatorname{eq}(C_n^k) \leq 1 + 2\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil$.
